test_title: PYST 2: SSC MTS 2023 - General Knowledge (Held On: 01 Sept, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following statements is correct about Article 129 of the Constitution of India?

options.text: It provides for the Supreme Court to give advisory opinion to the President.
It provides for the Supreme Court to be a court of original jurisdiction
It provides for the Supreme Court to be a court of record.
It provides for the Supreme Court to be the highest court of appeal.

solution:
The correct answer is **It provides for the Supreme Court to be a court of record.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 129** of the Constitution of India declares the Supreme Court to be a **court of record**. This status grants it two main powers: the power to punish for contempt of itself and the power to have its judgments recorded for perpetual memory and testimony.
 
• The option stating **"It provides for the Supreme Court to give advisory opinion to the President"** refers to **Article 143**, not Article 129, hence it is incorrect.
 
• The option that mentions **"It provides for the Supreme Court to be a court of original jurisdiction"** partially describes Article 131, which deals with the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court but does not fully encapsulate the provisions of Article 129. Therefore, it is not the best answer in this context.
 
• The statement about the Supreme Court being the **"highest court of appeal"** is true but is a more general characteristic of the Supreme Court and not specific to Article 129.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Supreme Court of India** has a wide range of functions and powers under the Constitution, including original jurisdiction, appellate jurisdiction, and advisory functions.
 
• As a **court of record**, the Supreme Court's judgments are of evidentiary value and cannot be questioned when produced before any court. They are recognized as legal precedents and sources of law.
 
• The role of the Supreme Court as the **highest court of appeal** covers appeals in civil, criminal, and constitutional cases, ensuring a unified interpretation of the law across India.

Hence, the statement about **Article 129** providing for the Supreme Court to be a court of record is correct
